title: 132 people thrown overboard — why was it never a murder trial?
description:
In 1781, the crew of the slave ship Zong threw at least 132 enslaved Africans into the Atlantic Ocean over several days, claiming the ship was low on water. Some victims leaped into the sea rather than wait to be seized.

No captain, crew member, or ship owner was ever charged with murder. Instead, Liverpool ship owners sued their insurers for the value of the lost "cargo" — thirty pounds per person. The case, Gregson versus Gilbert, treated human lives the same as jettisoned horses.

The victims' names were never recorded. Only the tonnage was. No one was ever punished.
